# An all-template obstruction to the shape-aware shell certificate

This note excludes a precisely defined sufficient-certificate menu. It
does not refute OC. The example has nonaffine fiber centroids, permits
every centroided convex template, every affine copy-center map, every
choice of contained radii, every integer anchor, and even exact own-fiber
depth in the certificate. The original body has a separate explicit
all-halfspace certificate satisfying OC.

## 1. The certificate being tested

For a full-dimensional convex body J in R^d with centroid zero and volume
V>0, write

  F_u(s)=|J intersect {x:u.x>=s}|/V,
  beta(J)=inf_(u!=0) F_u(0),
  kappa(J)=(1/2) inf_(u!=0,s in R)[F_u(s)+F_u(-s)].

Always 0<=beta(J)<=1/2 and 0<=kappa(J)<=1/2. The first upper bound
follows from the two complementary through-zero caps, whose fractions
sum to one. The second follows by taking |s| beyond the support in any
fixed direction, when the two tails sum to one. The proved ordinary
paired-tail theorem additionally gives kappa(J)>=Gamma_d, and ordinary
Grunbaum gives beta(J)>=Gamma_d, although these lower bounds will not
be needed for the obstruction.

Let a be any affine map from the integer-coordinate space to R^d, and
retain contained copies a(z)+r_z J in the original fibers, with r_z>=0.
At an actual anchor Y=(p,a(p)), put w_z=r_z^d. Let D_p(w) be the raw
weighted atomic depth on the integer base, and let R_p(w) be the sum of
min(w_z,w_(2p-z)) over distinct unordered reflected pairs. These are the
same definitions, including closed caps and zero radii, as in
`candidate 4d7e8cb4ef98b96f`.

Its disjoint-copy and annulus proof with the exact shape constants gives
the valid certificate

  V[beta(J) D_p(w)+(2 kappa(J)-beta(J)) R_p(w)].      (1)

Indeed, the equal inner pairs pay 2 kappa, the own core and captured
annuli pay beta, and the exact atomic identity is
D_p(w)=w_p+R_p(w)+D_p(residual). One may strengthen (1) by replacing the
own-core term with the exact ordinary raw depth delta_p of the original
own fiber at a(p). The resulting certificate is

  delta_p+V[beta(J)(D_p(w)-w_p)
                    +(2 kappa(J)-beta(J))R_p(w)].    (2)

Formula (2) dominates (1), since the original own fiber contains the
core and hence delta_p>=beta(J)Vw_p. Pure-integer caps remain valid:
each equal pair pays its full single-copy volume, at least 2 kappa V
times its weight, and a captured shell pays its full volume, at least
beta V times its weight. Thus (1), (2) do not omit those caps.

The menu tested below permits (2) for EVERY template, affine map,
contained set of radii, and actual integer anchor. It also permits the
ordinary own-fiber guarantee alone (the zero-other-core case). It does
not retain independent shape information from the original unpaired
fibers outside the chosen copies, and does not assert that every known
depth certificate belongs to this menu.

## 2. Two centered boxes with small common-copy capacity

Set d=200, m=100, and a=21/20. Let B be the centered unit box in R^d.
Let A be the centered box with side lengths a in coordinates 1,...,m
and 1/a in coordinates m+1,...,2m. Thus |A|=|B|=1. Put

  K_0=(A+B)/2,
  k=|K_0|=[(a+1)^2/(4a)]^m=(1681/1680)^100,
  t=a^(-m)=(20/21)^100.                              (3)

The following bounds are fully elementary and strict:

  1<k<16/15,          0<t<1/100,         Gamma_d>4/11. (4)

For the k bound, the finite binomial expansion and binom(100,j)<=100^j
give

  k < sum_(j>=0)(100/1680)^j=84/79<16/15.

The final comparison is 1260<1264. For t, the first seven terms give

  (21/20)^100 >= sum_(j=0)^6 binom(100,j)/20^j
                   =4209933/40000>100.

Finally (1+1/d)^d<e by termwise binomial comparison with the exponential
series. That series has first four terms 8/3, and its remaining tail is
at most (1/24) sum_(j>=0)5^(-j)=5/96. Thus
e<=87/32<11/4 and Gamma_d=(1+1/d)^(-d)>4/11.

Here is the bound that accounts for ALL templates and placements.
Suppose translates of r_- J and r_+ J are contained in A and B.
Let r=min(r_-,r_+). In every coordinate, the width of rJ is at most
the smaller of the two box side lengths, since widths are translation
invariant and scale linearly under homothety. The volume of any body
is at most the product of its coordinate widths, by containment in its
coordinate bounding box. Therefore

  V min(w_-,w_+)=|rJ|<=1^m(1/a)^m=t.                (5)

This does not assume that the two translated copies overlap. It does
not assume J is a box, centrally symmetric, polyhedral, or aligned in
any manner. Coordinate widths bound every convex template.

## 3. A small asymmetric addition and actual fibers

Let epsilon=1/1000. The first side length of K_0 is L_1=(a+1)/2.
Its facet at x_1=L_1/2 has (d-1)-volume F=k/L_1. Add the point

  v=(L_1/2+h,0,...,0),       h=d epsilon/F>0,
  K=conv(K_0 union {v}).

The point v lies strictly beyond that one facet and strictly inside
the halfspaces defining every other facet of K_0. Thus K minus K_0,
up to its null boundary, is the pyramid over that facet with apex v.
Its volume is Fh/d=epsilon. Consequently

  |K|=k+epsilon.                                      (6)

The first moment of K_0 is zero. The added pyramid has positive first
coordinate everywhere in its interior, so the centroid of K has
strictly positive first coordinate. Its other centroid coordinates
are zero by reflection symmetry in coordinates 2,...,d.

Now take the actual convex body in R times R^d

  C=conv( {-1} times A, {0} times K, {1} times B ).

Its projection is [-1,1] and its three integer fibers are exactly A,K,B.
The two extreme fibers remain A,B. At base zero, the only extra endpoint
interpolations lie in (A+B)/2=K_0 subset K, so the middle fiber is exactly
K. All are full dimensional, and C has ambient interior. Thus q=d and
the relevant original intrinsic mass is

  M=2+k+epsilon.                                     (7)

The endpoint centroids are zero and the middle centroid is nonzero,
so this actual family has a nonaffine centroid graph.

For EVERY continuous point y, the ordinary raw depth of K at y is at
most

  delta_K(y)<=k/2+epsilon.                            (8)

Indeed, the two complementary closed halfspaces through y in any fixed
nonzero direction have K_0 masses summing to k, since their boundary is
null. At least one has mass at most k/2, and the addition contributes
at most epsilon. That halfspace contains y and proves (8), whether or
not y belongs to K_0. Similarly the maximum ordinary depth of either
endpoint box is at most 1/2.

## 4. The complete optimized menu falls short

Consider ANY admissible template, affine center map and retained copies.
At the middle anchor p=0, exact atomic depth and reflection are

  D_0(w)=w_0+min(w_-,w_+),   R_0(w)=min(w_-,w_+).

The strongest version (2) therefore equals

  delta_K(a(0))+2 kappa(J) V min(w_-,w_+)
       <= k/2+epsilon+t
       < 8/15+1/1000+1/100=1633/3000.                (9)

Here (5), (8), and kappa(J)<=1/2 account for all templates and centers.
At either endpoint anchor, a base halfspace isolates that endpoint.
Hence D_p(w)=w_p and R_p(w)=0, and (2) is only its ordinary own-fiber
depth, at most 1/2. Zero radii and missing copies satisfy the same bounds.

In contrast, the original OC raw target satisfies, by (4), (7),

  (Gamma_d/2)M > (4/11)(3/2)=6/11.

The whole optimized menu, including every actual anchor, is thus strictly
below the required original target, by a uniform gap greater than

  6/11-1633/3000=37/33000>0.                          (10)

This is not only an obstruction to using the universal constant Gamma
on the common template: (9) already allows its best paired-tail constant
and exact ordinary own-fiber depth.

## 5. The original body has an explicit good point

Take Y=(0,0), which belongs to its middle box K_0 and hence to S.
Every through-Y ambient halfspace with nonzero continuous normal has
middle contribution at least k/2, since K_0 is centrally symmetric.
The continuous thresholds at the two centered endpoint boxes are opposite.
At least one is nonpositive, so that endpoint contributes at least 1/2.
The original raw captured mass is consequently at least

  (k+1)/2 > (Gamma_d/2)(k+epsilon+2).

For the strict comparison it suffices that Gamma_d<=1/2 and k>epsilon:
the difference from (k+epsilon+2)/4 is (k-epsilon)/4>0.
A pure-integer through-Y cap contains the whole middle fiber and at
least one endpoint, giving a larger bound. Every containing cap contains
the parallel through-Y cap. Thus Y is an actual deterministic OC point
for this family. No global central symmetry of S is asserted: A and B
are different, and the middle fiber has an asymmetric addition.

## 6. Binary padding gives every integer rank

For any n>=1, take C_n=[0,1]^(n-1) times C with the first n coordinates
integer. A reflected pair at an integer anchor stays in its binary block,
since two bits have a binary midpoint only when both equal that midpoint.
Thus R_p(w) has exactly the same within-block possibilities as above.

The weighted atomic depth D_p(w) is at most the corresponding depth in
that block. To see this, choose a strict linear functional exposing its
binary vertex and multiply it by a sufficiently large coefficient, then
add either of the two chain directions. Finiteness of the retained bases
ensures that every other binary block is excluded while the desired
within-block sign pattern is retained. This is an actual base halfspace,
not a change to the original weights. Hence the upper bounds in (9)
remain valid for every affine map on all n coordinates and every anchor.

The original mass is 2^(n-1)M and its OC target is still Gamma_d M/2.
An explicit good point in any binary block has the bound in Section 5;
other blocks can only add mass. Consequently the same exact obstruction
to the optimized single-template certificate, and the same independent
OC-safe calibration, hold in every n>=1 with d=200.
